answer: Because the relic index resolves every citation against the tundra checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the walnut audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 125 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 125 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
